question: Should OpenClaw own this grouped Claw update planner as an experiment-gated core lifecycle contract, rather than leaving the workflow to a plugin or external package surface?
rationale: The branch introduces a new core command, a versioned planner result, and consent semantics across persisted state, workspace content, packages, MCP declarations, and cron declarations; code review alone cannot establish the intended long-term product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core experiment
options.body: Accept the read-only planner as a gated core primitive after the prerequisite diagnostics slice lands and current-head redaction proof is posted.

options.title: Keep the lifecycle outside core
options.body: Pause this stack and define only the extension seams needed for a plugin-owned or external implementation.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Leave the PR open without merging until the RFC and owner boundary receive a maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core experiment
recommendation.body: Accept the read-only planner as a gated core primitive after the prerequisite diagnostics slice lands and current-head redaction proof is posted.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and authored the concrete review requirements for the lifecycle planning boundary.
